[Thinking]
**Calculating square root approximation**

I'm working through the square of 15.467 and calculating different nearby values. Initially, my estimates were a bit off, so I adjusted my increments. I determined 15.463 was too low and 15.466 too high. Eventually, I found that 15.4645 gave a value slightly above what I targeted. I calculated the necessary adjustment, landing around 15.464245, which I rounded to 15.464 for clarity. Now, I'll present the solution neatly boxed!
[/Thinking]

Mean = (25+10+0+9−1−14−21)/7 = 8/7.

Sum of squared deviations = Σ(xi − 8/7)^2 = 70308/49.

Sample variance = (70308/49)/(7−1) = 70308/294 = 239.142857...

Sample standard deviation = sqrt(239.142857...) ≈ 15.464.

Final answer: \boxed{15.464\text{ (approximately)}}
